post.description: Takes a consistent copy of the database while Bayplan runs and answers with it as a download named bayplan-backup-<UTC YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.bayplan, locked with the passphrase in the body. The backup holds users, teams, access, settings, environments and the audit log. It does not hold the master key, sessions, invite or reset links or pending join tokens, and every secret in it is sealed under a key that is only inside the encrypted file. The passphrase is sent in the body, is never stored or logged, and is not in the audit entry. 422 passphrase_too_short for fewer than 16 characters; 409 audit_chain_broken when the audit log does not verify; 409 backup_busy while another backup is being prepared. Audited as backup.exported. Needs backup.manage.
post.summary: Download an encrypted backup

get.description: The shortest passphrase a backup accepts, the file extension a backup file has and the largest file a restore accepts. Needs backup.manage.

post.description: Replaces everything in this Bayplan with the uploaded backup. The backup is opened, migrated to this version, re-keyed to this instance's master key and verified on a private copy first; nothing live changes until all of that has worked. Then Bayplan saves the current database as backups/prerestore-<time>.db, swaps the restored one in and restarts itself. The answer is 202 and Bayplan is unreachable for a moment; everyone is signed out, including the caller. confirm must be this instance's name (422 confirm_mismatch). The same refusals as the check apply and leave everything as it was. Audited in the restored log as audit.reanchored then backup.restored. Needs backup.manage.
post.summary: Restore an uploaded backup over this instance

post.description: Opens the uploaded file with the passphrase and answers what is in it, without changing anything. 422 backup_unreadable for a wrong passphrase or a damaged file, 422 not_a_backup for a file that is not a backup, 409 backup_newer for a backup from a newer Bayplan, 404 upload_not_found for an upload that is gone or expired, 409 restore_busy while another check or restore runs. Audited as backup.checked. Needs backup.manage.

A revoked environment says nothing here. Errors come first, then the newest. Names are at most 64 characters.

delete.description: Needs environments.delete. Stops managing the host. Revokes every agent, disables the join token and deletes the environment, and changes nothing in Docker: its containers, networks and volumes are untouched (D-20, D-30). With uninstallAgents=true each online agent is first told to uninstall itself (a swarm's agents through one manager, which removes the agent service and its token secret; every agent removes its own container and state volume), and the request waits up to 30 seconds for their answers. Whatever they answer, or do not, the revoking and deletion follow, so hosts that were offline or refused keep their agent until the admin runs the manual cleanup command that GET /api/env/{envId}/agents gives. Audited as environment.removed, agent.revoked per agent, and agent.uninstalled per agent that confirmed.

post.description: Makes a new join token and retires the current one in the same transaction. The old install command stops enrolling hosts at once; agents that are already enrolled keep their certificates and are not disconnected. Answers the install object for the new token, once, with Cache-Control no-store; when the environment is a swarm that already has agents it carries the one-line rotate command. 404 environment_not_found; 409 public_url_required when Bayplan has no address to give agents, and 409 insecure_agent_url when that address is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off; the current token stays in both cases. Needs environments.token. Audited as environment.token_rotated with the new generation.
post.summary: Rotate an environment's join token

get.summary: Get the instance name, whether setup is needed and the remember-me length

post.description: Public. Spends the link and sets the user's password. It does not sign anyone in: the user signs in afterwards with the password they chose. A link works once.
post.summary: Choose a password with a one-time link

post.description: Public. The token is in the body, never in the address. Every link that cannot be used, whether expired, used, replaced, unknown or belonging to a disabled or deleted user, answers the same 404 invalid_link.
post.summary: Say what a one-time link is for

get.description: Reports whether a Docker socket exists at the configured path and, if so, what engine answers on it: supported or not (and why), its version and API version, and whether the host is a Swarm manager, a Swarm worker or standalone. Read-only. Needs environments.create because it is the context for adding the host.
get.summary: Detect the Docker engine on this server's own host
Get the signed-in user, their CSRF token and their effective permissions

post.description: Needs the current password. On success every session of the user ends, this one included, and a new session starts: its cookie is set and its CSRF token returned (D-32, D-34). A wrong current password or a new password that breaks the policy answers 422 with a stable code per field. Attempts are throttled per user and the refusal is 429 rate_limited. Audited as auth.password_changed.
post.summary: Change the signed-in user's own password

get.description: The username, display name and email, with the updatedAt a save must be based on.
get.summary: Read the signed-in user's own profile

patch.description: Send displayName, email or both, with the updatedAt you read. If the profile changed since, nothing is saved and the answer is 409 stale_change. The username can never be changed and is not accepted. An invalid field answers 422 on body.displayName or body.email. Saving what is already there changes nothing. Audited as user.updated with the caller as actor and target.
patch.summary: Edit the signed-in user's own display name and email

get.description: Up to 3 environment IDs, the most recently used first and, for uses at the same instant, in ID order. An environment that was removed, or that the user can no longer read, is left out.
get.summary: The environments the signed-in user used last

put.description: Sets the environment's last-used time to now. Using the same environment again keeps one entry with the newer time. Only the newest 3 per user are kept. An environment that does not exist and one the user cannot read both answer 404 environment_not_found, so the answer never says which exist.
put.summary: Record that the signed-in user used an environment

get.description: Every browser the caller is signed in on, most recently active first, with the device, address and last activity, and current set on the one making this request.
get.summary: List the signed-in user's sessions

post.description: Ends every session of the caller except the one making this request, and says how many ended. Audited as user.sessions_revoked.
post.summary: Sign out everywhere else

delete.description: That browser's next request answers 401. The session making this request cannot be revoked here: 409 current_session. A handle that is not one of the caller's sessions answers 404 session_not_found. Audited as session.revoked.

get.description: publicUrlLocked is true when the BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL environment variable fixes the public URL (D-04), agentUrlLocked when BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL fixes the agent URL (D-18). agentEndpoint is the address agents dial: the agent URL, else the public URL, with its path and /agent/connect. enrolledAgents counts the agents that are not revoked and offlineAgents those of them with no connection now (D-19). agentEndpointRefused is true when agentEndpoint is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off: agents cannot connect to it (G-02-R4-3).
get.summary: Get the instance name, public URL and agent URL

patch.description: Only the fields sent are changed. Invalid fields answer 422 with a stable code per field (instance_name_required, instance_name_too_long, invalid_public_url, invalid_agent_url, insecure_agent_url). An agent URL that is plain http for a host that is not this machine answers 422 insecure_agent_url unless BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is on, because agents refuse such an address; a loopback or https agent URL, clearing it, and an http public URL are accepted. A different public URL while BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL is set answers 409 public_url_locked, and a different agent URL while BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL is set answers 409 agent_url_locked; both change nothing. An empty agentUrl clears it. A change takes effect at once: the Origin check and the cookie Secure flag use the new public URL from the next request. When the address agents dial changes, every agent connected over a TLS-verified session is sent the new address and the server's pins over its tunnel and dials that address from its next connection; an agent takes only a wss:// address this way. From then on the server accepts agent handshakes only for the new host and port, with no fallback period: an agent that was offline or on plain ws:// at the time is refused auth_rejected until it is reinstalled with the new address or the change is reverted. Each change is audited as settings.updated with the old and new value of every changed field.
patch.summary: Change the instance name, the public URL or the agent URL

post.description: Needs the setup token. Runs once: it creates the admin, assigns the global admin role, stores the instance name and public URL, starts a session and audits setup.completed in one transaction, then consumes the token. A second call answers 409 setup_complete.
post.summary: Create the first admin, store the instance settings and sign in
Check the setup token and return the step 3 defaults

get.description: Every team, sorted by name ignoring case, with how many members and grants each has. Only an instance admin may manage teams.
get.summary: List teams

post.description: A team name is 1 to 64 characters and unique ignoring case: a name another team holds answers 409 team_name_taken and an empty or too long one answers 422 on body.name. Audited as team.created.
post.summary: Create a team

delete.description: Removes the team, its grants and its memberships in one step, so no assignment or membership is left pointing at it. Its members lose the access it gave them on their next request, and the automations they own that no longer qualify pause. The answer lists who lost which access, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one team.deleted entry carrying members, impact_count and impact: the first ten items "username: environment before→after" joined by "; " and cut to 512 bytes. An unknown team answers 404 team_not_found.

get.description: The team with its members sorted by username. An unknown team answers 404 team_not_found.
get.summary: Read one team and its members

patch.description: Send the name with the updatedAt you read. If the team changed since, nothing is saved and the answer is 409 stale_change. A name another team holds, ignoring case, answers 409 team_name_taken; an empty or too long one answers 422 on body.name. Saving the name it already has changes nothing. Audited as team.renamed with the old name.

get.description: The grants made to the team: the one on every environment first, then those on single environments by name. Every member holds what they give. An unknown team answers 404 team_not_found.
get.summary: List a team's grants

put.description: As putUserGrant, for a team: every member holds the role (the highest across their sources). An unknown team answers 404 team_not_found.
put.summary: Give a team a role on an environment

delete.description: As deleteUserGrant, for a grant made to a team: every member loses what it gave them.

post.description: As previewUserGrantImpact, for a grant made to a team: the impact is on every member.
post.summary: Preview what removing or changing a team's grant takes away

post.description: Works out, with the same evaluator that enforces access, who would lose which environment access if the team were deleted (op delete) or a member removed (op remove_member, with userId). The change is applied inside a transaction that is rolled back, so nothing is written and nothing is audited. Confirming recomputes the impact when it commits. A remove_member for a user who is not in the team answers 404 member_not_found.
post.summary: Preview who loses access if a team changes

post.description: All or none: a user who does not exist or is deleted answers 404 user_not_found and nothing is added. A user who is already in the team changes nothing and writes no audit entry. Each user added is audited as team.member_added. Membership never makes anyone an instance admin.
post.summary: Add users to a team

delete.description: The user loses the access the team gave them on their next request and keeps every other grant. The automations they own that no longer qualify pause. The answer lists what they lost, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one team.member_removed entry carrying impact_count and impact (first ten items "username: environment before→after" joined by "; ", cut to 512 bytes). A user who is not in the team answers 404 member_not_found and nothing is written.
delete.summary: Remove a user from a team

get.description: Every user who is not deleted, sorted by username, with the status the users table shows: locked, disabled, invite expired, invite pending or active, in that order of precedence.
get.summary: List users

post.description: The user has no password. The response carries a link, valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL (72 hours by default), that opens a page where they choose one. Bayplan sends no email: the admin hands the link over. A username that belonged to a deleted user answers 409 username_reserved.
post.summary: Create a user and a one-time invite link

delete.description: Turns the user into a tombstone and cannot be undone: they are disabled, their password, email and display name are cleared, instance admin is turned off, and their sessions, links, direct access and team memberships are removed in one step. Their username stays reserved, so creating it again answers 409 username_reserved. The automations they own pause as owner deleted, except those listed in the optional reassign body, which go to the user named for each in the same step; a user who could not run one answers 422 owner_not_eligible, one that is not the deleted user's answers 404 automation_not_found, and nothing is deleted. The last active instance admin cannot be deleted: 409 last_instance_admin. A user who is already deleted answers 404 user_not_found.

get.description: The user as the user page shows them. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: Read one user

patch.description: Send displayName, email or both, with the updatedAt you read. If the user changed since, nothing is saved and the answer is 409 stale_change. The username can never be changed and is not accepted. An invalid field answers 422 on body.displayName or body.email. Saving what is already there changes nothing.
patch.summary: Edit a user's display name and email

get.description: The user's effective access: for each environment the user can reach, the highest role any source gives, the union of the extra permissions and every source (instance, all, team, direct), computed by the same evaluator that enforces access. An instance admin holds every environment, so the list is empty and instanceAdmin is true. grants lists the user's own grants, the ones editable on the user page. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: What a user may do on each environment, and why

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once and refuses their sign-in. Their grants and team memberships are kept and the automations they own pause. Answers the user as they now are. Disabling a disabled user changes nothing. The last active instance admin cannot be disabled: 409 last_instance_admin.
post.summary: Disable a user

post.description: Lets a disabled user sign in again with the grants and teams they had. Enabling an enabled user changes nothing.
post.summary: Enable a user

put.description: Gives the user Admin, Operator or Viewer on one environment (scope env, with envId) or on all of them (scope all). A user holds at most one grant per scope: saving an existing combination edits it (200, audited as access.updated), a new one is created (201, access.granted). Extras are accepted only on Operator: a Viewer answers 422 viewer_cannot_have_extras, an Admin 422 extras_implied and a permission that is not an extra 422 unknown_extra. With expected set, a grant that has changed answers 409 stale_change. A grant never expires. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found and an unknown environment 404 environment_not_found.
put.summary: Give a user a role on an environment

delete.description: Removes the grant. The user loses the access it gave on their next request and keeps every other grant, and the automations they own that no longer qualify pause. The answer lists who lost which access, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one access.revoked entry carrying the subject, role, scope, impact_count and impact. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.

post.description: Works out, with the same evaluator that enforces access, who would lose which environment access if the grant were deleted (op delete) or saved with a lower role (op update, with role and extras). The change is applied inside a transaction that is rolled back, so nothing is written and nothing is audited. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.
post.summary: Preview what removing or changing a user's grant takes away

post.description: Instance authority belongs to a user, never to a team. Setting what is already set changes nothing. Turning it off for the last active instance admin answers 409 last_instance_admin. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Turn instance admin on or off for a user

post.description: For a user who has not yet set a password. The new link replaces the previous one, which stops working at once, and is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL. A user who has already set a password answers 409 not_invited; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
post.summary: Replace a user's invite link

get.description: The git syncs and webhooks that run with the user's permissions, with the environment each acts on and whether it is active or paused because its owner was disabled, deleted or no longer holds the permission it needs. Empty when they own nothing. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List the automations a user owns

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once, in the same step that makes the link, and answers a one-time link built like an invite's that lets them choose a new password. It is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL (72 hours by default) and replaces any link they held. Bayplan sends no email: the admin hands the link over. A disabled user answers 409 user_disabled; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.password_reset_issued with the number of sessions ended.
post.summary: Issue a password reset link

get.description: For an admin on a user's page. No session is marked current. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List a user's sessions

post.description: Signs the user out everywhere at once and says how many ended. Nothing is written when they were not signed in anywhere. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.sessions_revoked.
post.summary: End all of a user's sessions

post.description: Clears the lock and the failed sign-in count, audited as auth.unlocked with the caller as actor. A user who is not locked is left alone and nothing is audited. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Unlock a locked user

get.summary: Get the running Bayplan version and source link

get.description: Includes data_not_persisted while the data directory would be lost with the container, and key_backup while the encryption key Bayplan generated into the data directory has not been acknowledged (D-15, D-59). The reverse proxy warnings (the proxy_ ones) are listed while Bayplan has seen that problem in the last hour, one item per kind, naming the newest sighting (D-53). refusal_burst lists, for instance admins only, each user who was refused ten or more times in a minute in the last hour (D-20). The plain-HTTP warning is the browser's to compute and is not listed.
get.summary: List the instance warnings that need an admin's attention

post.description: Records, once for the whole instance, that the generated encryption key has been backed up, and audits it as warning.acknowledged.
post.summary: Acknowledge the encryption key backup reminder
